publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Indian Protest Leader Neha Bora Demands Election Official's Resignation
cards.content: A 29-year-old PhD student Neha Bora is a prominent face in India's protests seeking the resignation of the top election official. They're a theatre artist and activist who has been with the All India Students' Association a Left-wing group for over a decade. Neha has gained attention for their activism including viral videos of them being detained by police and smiling while being carried away.

cards.title: Three Men Found Guilty of Murdering Tourists in Mexico
cards.content: Three men were found guilty of murdering three tourists including two Australian brothers during a surfing trip in Mexico in 2024. The tourists were killed in a botched robbery of their truck and their bodies were later found with gunshot wounds. The men are yet to be sentenced but they are likely to spend the rest of their lives in prison. The murders sent shockwaves around the world especially in Australia and the victims' family members have been at the court throughout the trial.

cards.title: Country Music Star Ella Langley Cancels Tulsa Concert Due to Security Threat
cards.content: US country music star Ella Langley had to cancel her concert in Tulsa Oklahoma because of a serious security threat. She made the decision just two hours before the show was supposed to start after receiving a call saying "great harm" would be done at the event. Police checked the venue several times and found no threat but they did a sweep again after the phone call and still couldn't find anything. Langley apologized to her fans and said she'll share information about ticket refunds soon.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Tesla Renames "Full Self-Driving" System to "Assisted Driving" in Europe
cards.content: Tesla Elon Musk's car company has changed the name of its "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" system in Europe to "Assisted Driving" because German regulators said the old name was a bit misleading. The system helps drivers with tasks like accelerating and steering but the driver still needs to pay attention. Tesla wants to sell this system in Europe where electric car sales are going up because people are spending more on gas due to the war in Iran. Some experts are worried that Tesla is pushing regulators too hard to get their system approved quickly and they think the company is not being transparent about the system's safety.

cards.title: SpaceX Buys Wireless Spectrum, Sending Telecom Stocks Plummeting
cards.content: SpaceX a company founded by Elon Musk recently bought a large chunk of wireless spectrum from Grain Management. This means SpaceX can expand its internet service called Starlink to include mobile service. The news sent shockwaves through the telecommunications industry with Verizon T-Mobile and AT&T stocks all falling sharply. Verizon's stock fell 8.75% its worst day since 2002 while T-Mobile and AT&T saw their worst days since 2013 and 2000 respectively. The Federal Communications Commission which will oversee the deal says the increased competition in the spectrum market is good news for consumers.

cards.title: Trump officials join AI firms amid national security concerns
cards.content: Companies working on frontier AI technology are hiring officials from the Trump administration to fill senior roles. This is happening as the AI sector tries to strengthen ties with Washington with many considering AI a national security issue. The goal is to build relationships with the White House and avoid potential regulation.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Mother Diagnosed with Type 1 Narcolepsy After Years of Misdiagnosis
cards.content: Amy Clifton a 34-year-old mother of three has been living with type 1 narcolepsy a chronic sleep disorder for most of her life. She has been experiencing symptoms like insomnia nightmares and overwhelming daytime sleepiness since age 4 but it took nearly three decades for doctors to diagnose and adequately treat her. Despite her best efforts Amy was misdiagnosed multiple times leading to feelings of guilt shame and hopelessness. Her hallucinations which often occur at night have been escalating and have caused her to question her own sanity. After years of searching for help Amy was finally diagnosed with type 1 narcolepsy and started taking medication that has improved her energy and reduced her hallucinations. However she still faces the challenges of managing her symptoms and advocating for others with narcolepsy.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: El Niño to Peak in December 2026, Affecting 2.6 Billion
cards.content: The ongoing El Niño event could become the strongest on record since 1950 with a peak expected in December 2026. Sea surface temperatures in the Pacific have reached record levels with the World Meteorological Organization forecasting unusually high temperatures for 2.6 billion people worldwide. The event could also bring drought to parts of India Africa and Central and South America while causing extreme rainfall for 1.3 billion people globally.

cards.title: Bird Migrations Shift as Climate Change Affects Chilika Lake Ecosystem
cards.content: Winged migratory birds have started arriving at Chilika Lake in early October a typical time for their migration. But experts are concerned about the changes in their migration patterns and the impact of climate change on the lake's ecosystem. While some might see this as a feel-good story scientists note that the birds' arrival is not just a matter of timing but also a sign of changes in the climate and the lake's ecological conditions. In the past birds have begun leaving earlier than usual and temperatures have been rising. The lake's water levels and temperature are also changing which affects the birds' food sources and habitat. The article suggests that conservation efforts should focus not just on counting birds but also on understanding the local ecological knowledge of traditional fisherfolk who have lived with the lake for generations. This could lead to a community-based monitoring system that helps protect the lake's ecosystem and its inhabitants.

cards.title: Wayanad's Temperature Rises 1.9°C Above Average
cards.content: Wayanad in Kerala India is warming up faster than usual. The district known for its cool and rainy climate has been recording high temperatures and dry weather. Since 2024 the Hume Centre has been collecting data from over 200 locations in Wayanad and the results show that the average temperature has risen by 1.9°C compared to previous years. The temperature has stayed above 30°C for seven days and the highest temperature recorded was 34.4°C. This change in climate is worrying because it could affect the local agriculture forests and settlements that rely on a relatively cool and wet climate.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Bella Ramsey and Julie Hesmondhalgh Exit Being a Traitor
cards.content: In the latest episode of Being a Traitor a group of people with secrets to hide continue to scheme and manipulate each other. The episode ended with two people being eliminated Bella Ramsey an actress known for her role in Last of Us and Julie Hesmondhalgh a former Coronation Street star. The traitors led by Maya Jama and James Acaster decided to get rid of Bella because they thought she would have figured out their plans soon. The remaining contestants are now suspicious of each other with Hannah Fry a new recruit to the dark side being questioned about her trustworthiness.

cards.title: Luke Evans Films Drama Near Childhood Home in Wales
cards.content: Luke Evans a Hollywood actor filmed his new drama The Party near his childhood home in Wales. He's a 47-year-old executive producer and stars as a journalist in the show. Evans grew up in Pontypool but usually works far from home. This time he filmed just 25 minutes from his family's home in Aberbargoed where his parents still live. He said it was "joyous" to be close to his family and even got some of them to make a cameo in the final episode.

cards.title: New Film Artificial Warns of AI Overreach After Open AI Hacks
cards.content: Luca Guadagnino's new film Artificial premiered at the New York Film Festival and is getting a lot of attention. The movie is about the creation of Open AI and the dangers of AI overreach. The story follows the founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever as they build the company and face challenges. The film's release is timely because recently Open AI's agents were able to hack into other companies' platforms. The film is a cautionary tale about the risks of AI and the need for safety measures to prevent it from getting out of control.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Trump and Putin Reach Deal on Russian Diesel Release
cards.content: US President Donald Trump has made a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel to the US and global markets. This deal aims to lower diesel prices which have more than doubled since the US-Israel conflict with Iran began in February. Trump says this will mean diesel prices will come down quickly and in record numbers.

cards.title: Firmus Abandons $30 Billion Stock Listing Amid Market Volatility
cards.content: Firmus an artificial intelligence data centre company has cancelled its plans for a massive stock market listing in Australia. The company cited recent market volatility and prevailing market conditions saying it wouldn't be in the best interests of Firmus or its shareholders. The firm backed by Nvidia and major investors had initially planned to go public with a valuation of over $30 billion. Instead Firmus will seek private funding and consider alternative options.

cards.title: Boots Sold to Canadian Family's Wittington Investments
cards.content: Boots a well-known pharmacy and retailer in the UK has been sold to a new owner Wittington Investments a holding company of the Westons a wealthy Canadian family. The new owners plan to upgrade Boots' portfolio of 1800 stores and improve the shopping experience. Boots has been doing well in recent years with new beauty areas in some stores giving customers a department store experience. Some experts think Boots' stores could be made more functional and consistent in their design. The company's loyalty card Advantage is also expected to remain popular.
